app_size_assumptions.model_note: saanoTTS int8 blobs = 679,832 B (paper). 0xC0000 = 768 KB gives 16 % headroom. Peak tensor arena ~289 KB lives in RAM/PSRAM, not flash.

OTA x2 slots, model in its own partition (shared by both slots)
OTA x2 slots, model linked into the app image (duplicated per slot)

flash_mmap_for_the_dictionary.verdict: YES - a read-only dictionary partition can be esp_partition_mmap()'d and read with ordinary random loads. This is exactly what Espressif's own on-device TTS does.

production_precedent.what: esp-skainet examples/chinese_tts maps a 3890 KB 'voice_data' partition and hands the raw pointer to the TTS library

why_the_paper's_SIMD_finding_does_not_tr: The paper's failure (correlation 0.011) was on SIMD/PIE operands for model weights - a sustained, aligned, high-bandwidth stream (45 MMAC per audio-second).
Dictionary lookup is the opposite regime: a few hundred scattered 4-16 B reads per utterance, via ordinary scalar loads through the D-cache.

The ESP32-S3 SoC Errata v1.3 lists 8 items ([CACHE-126], [RTC-126], [ANALOG-160], [LCD-239], [USBOTG-4289], [RMT-176], [TOUCH-100], [ADC-183]); NONE concerns PIE/vector loads from memory-mapped flash. [CACHE-126] is about cache WRITE-BACKS, which a read-only flash mapping never performs.
So the paper's collapse is not a documented silicon defect for read-only scalar access; treat it as specific to their PIE kernel path.

measured_access_cost.method: scratchpad/b0/trie_cost.py - instrumented Darts double-array common-prefix search over the REAL NAIST-JDIC sys.dic (788,923 entries), 300 sentences sampled (seed 0) from pool.tsv

worst_case_timing_estimate.assumption: every one of ~585 reads/sentence is a D-cache miss; 64 B line fill; QIO @ 80 MHz (4 data lines) = ~128 clk data + ~20 clk cmd/addr/dummy = ~148 clk = ~1.85 us
worst_case_timing_estimate.compare_decoder_compute: paper RTF 0.22 on S3 -> ~0.87 s of CPU per 3.96 s sentence; dictionary I/O is ~0.12 % of that
worst_case_timing_estimate.status: ESTIMATE - arithmetic from documented clocking, not measured on hardware

flash_mmap_for_the_dictionary.mmu_pressure: A dictionary partition of D MB needs D*16 MMU entries out of 512. A 4 MB dict = 64 entries; it can stay mapped for the whole life of the program, so there is no page churn and no remapping cost.
flash_mmap_for_the_dictionary.recommended_partition_type: raw custom data partition (or subtype 'fat'/'undefined' used raw). Do NOT put the dictionary in SPIFFS/LittleFS: those add per-file overhead and, more importantly, cannot be mmap'd - you would have to read()/copy into RAM.

sd_card_option.when: only if the dictionary must exceed the flash budget, or must be user-replaceable
sd_card_option.hardware: ESP32-S3 has 2 SDMMC slots (1-/4-bit) plus SPI-mode SD
sd_card_option.hard_constraint: SD content CANNOT be memory-mapped. ESP-IDF: 'mmap is supported by cache, so it can only be used on main flash.' Every dictionary probe becomes a block read through FATFS.

designs.name: D1 load-to-PSRAM at boot
designs.how: read the whole dict from SD into PSRAM once, then random-access it at PSRAM speed
designs.cost: needs dict_size <= PSRAM free space (8 MB PSRAM board: ~6-7 MB usable); boot delay ~1-3 s for a 4 MB dict at typical 2-5 MB/s SD throughput (UNMEASURED)

designs.name: D2 stream from SD per lookup
designs.how: keep the trie resident, page token/feature records from SD
designs.cost: ~585 block reads/sentence -> FATFS + SD latency (order 0.1-1 ms each) = 0.06-0.6 s/sentence
designs.verdict: borderline; would eat a real share of the 0.87 s compute budget

sd_card_option.downside: breaks the paper's 'general-purpose microcontroller, no external storage' claim; adds pins, cost, and an absent/corrupt-card failure mode

recommendation.target_board: ESP32-S3-WROOM-1-N16R8 (16 MB quad flash, 8 MB octal PSRAM, 3.3 V)
recommendation.why: 11.19 MB free for the dictionary WITH two OTA slots, 13.19 MB without OTA. 3.3 V quad flash keeps the board mainstream and cheap; 32 MB requires the 1.8 V octal WROOM-2 whose 8 GB-class variants are mostly EOL.
recommendation.dictionary_size_target: <= 4 MB. That fits every scenario on 16 MB and 32 MB, and fits 8 MB boards in scenarios A and B.
recommendation.8MB_verdict: viable but tight: 5.19 MB (no OTA) / 3.19 MB (OTA). An 8 MB board forces either OTA or a >3 MB dictionary to be dropped.
recommendation.32MB_verdict: not needed. Buys ~16 MB more headroom for a dictionary that should be <= 4 MB, at the price of 1.8 V octal flash and an EOL-heavy module line.
